scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8879: Users in both pods report that no internal portal
loads by NAME anymore -- web0.local through web3.local all fail with
name-resolution errors. Loading a portal directly by its IP address (e.g.
http://10.200.0.3) still works, and pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dns_server BIND (named) DNS service
Mechanism: the named daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) has been killed, so
  nothing answers on port 53 and every *.local lookup from the pods times
  out -- which is why the portals fail by name. Everything else is healthy:
  the host 10.200.0.2 itself is up and pingable, the OSPF path works, and
  the web servers keep serving HTTP (portals load when addressed by IP).
  The symptom is purely dead name resolution.
Localization: dns_server
Root cause: named not running on dns_server (port 53 closed)
Fix: `systemctl start named` on dns_server
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`).
Once named is answering again, web0.local..web3.local resolve to their
10.200.0.x addresses and the portals load by name. The web servers and the
network need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

agent.diagnosis_text:
The BIND9 named daemon on dns_server was not running at the time of the
report, causing port 53 on 10.200.0.2 to actively refuse connections.
Both hosts are correctly configured with "nameserver 10.200.0.2" in
/etc/resolv.conf, and the DNS server is IP-reachable (the interface holds
10.200.0.2/24 and pings succeed). However, every nslookup issued by the
hosts received "connection refused" on port 53 — not a timeout, an
immediate refusal — because no process was listening.

Inspection of dns_server showed the named service as "inactive (dead)"
while marked "enabled" in systemd. The zone file /etc/bind/db.local is
well-formed and complete (A records for web0–web3 mapping correctly to
10.200.0.3–10.200.0.6, and named-checkconf reported no errors), so the
fault is not in the DNS data itself. The startup script
(startup.sh) contains "systemctl start named", but systemd is not a
fully functional init inside Kathara/Docker containers; the systemctl
call either failed silently or the daemon exited immediately after the
container came up, leaving the service dead.

Running "service named start" brought the daemon up immediately (bind9
named -u bind), and name resolution from both pod hosts was confirmed
working for web0.local through web3.local.

Root cause: the dns_server startup script uses "systemctl start named",
which does not reliably start services inside Kathara containers, so the
BIND9 daemon was never running after lab deployment.

Corrective fix: Replace "systemctl start named" with "service named
start" (or invoke named directly: /usr/sbin/named -u bind) in
dns_server's startup script so the daemon starts reliably on every lab
launch.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies dns_server as the affected device.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identified that the BIND/named daemon on dns_server was not running (port 53 closed/connection refused), matching the required component identification.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken
per_axis.rationale: The report notes 10.200.0.2 is IP-reachable but does not explicitly state that portals/web servers load by IP, so it fails to fully rule out a network/webserver issue as required.
Replacing the failing systemctl call with 'service named start' or launching named directly ensures the BIND daemon is started, which matches the expected remediation to restart named.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations for the key claims (hosts point to 10.200.0.2, nslookup showed 'connection refused', named was inactive, named-checkconf/zone loaded, manual service start succeeded and restored resolution, startup script contains 'systemctl start named'). The only mildly speculative element is the claim that systemctl is nonfunctional in Kathara containers, but the observed facts (startup script attempts systemctl and service named was not running until manually started) support that inference well.
